analysis: Documentation-only PR across three files. docs/consumer/verification.md (head lines 64-69) adds a paragraph stating the provider's App Attest endpoint-resumption candidate proves custody of a process key on a fresh connection, is not new Apple proof or a consumer-verifiable credential, does not extend proof validity, and does not establish that the platform counterpart is deployed. docs/architecture/security/identity-binding.md (head lines 94-110) documents same-process endpoint resumption: K stays in process memory, answered once on the current socket via CoordinatorClient.answerAppAttestResume, and creates no local trust. It also adds sections on provider logout/token revocation (137-146) and erasure of APNs runtime state (159-176). docs/developer/build.md adds guidance for building a native serving qualification entry in a separate worktree, with no replacement of the installed app. The text is consistent with the TB-011, T-053, T-055 and T-056 assumptions: it expressly disclaims authorization extension and consumer verifiability, and notes that backend revocation, retention and authorization remain platform-owned. It makes no claim that weakens the existing serving, revocation or dispatch recheck model. Residual risk: the docs describe provider-side behavior (resume responder, logout revocation via POST /v1/device/revoke) whose code and coordinator counterparts were not supplied. Later passes should confirm the coordinator never treats the resume proof as grant extension, and that revocation and token-hash handling match the documented behavior. The threat model has no entry explicitly covering the endpoint-resumption candidate. That is a minor documentation-level gap, not a regression. No new attack surface was introduced by these changes.
